newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 16.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Mail plane banned before fatal crash: A mail plane that nosedived into the Tararua Ranges in June, killing the pilot, had been barred by the Civil Aviation Authority from making passenger or freight flights two weeks before the crash. Page 1.
Kopu to remain with Alliance in 'den of lions': Alliance MP Alamein Kopu has given an assurance that she will not quit the Alliance, but she criticised Parliament as a "den of lions". Page 1.
Don't use vote to punish -- ACT: ACT NZ has urged the public not to vote against the compulsory retirement savings scheme just to punish NZ First for its "shenanigans". Page 2.

NZ's low defence spending 'of concern' to US: New Zealand's low level of defence spending was of greater concern to the United States than the anti-nuclear policy, a senior United States government official said on Tuesday. Page 2.

Bolger renews support for new savings scheme: Prime Minister Jim Bolger renewed his support for Treasurer Winston Peters' compulsory superannuation scheme on Tuesday -- after State Services Minister Jenny Shipley delivered an attack on the policy. Page 2.
Inflation figure runs as forecast: Financial markets settled down on Tuesday after the consumer price index mirrored market expectations. Page 13.
Government charges add most, says Manfed: Inflation might be negative if government charges were not counted, the Manufacturers Federation said on Tuesday. Page 13.
Gas firms face disclosure: Gas companies would have to disclose cost and reliability details under new regulations designed to increase competition, Energy Max Bradford said on Tuesday. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Alliance faces new solidarity test: The Green Party is on the verge of creating a separate identity for itself outside the Alliance -- a challenge that will prove a far greater test of the five-party grouping than the crisis posed by MP Alamein Kopu.

Dearer petrol may fuel ACC cost drive: A petrol price rise of 5 cents a litre and hitting V8 boy racers with stiff car registration fees are among proposals floated by a National Minister to pin a greater part of the cost of road accidents on high-risk motorists.

Expansion plans but no moves on petrol: Fletcher Challenge has confirmed it has investigated expanding bulk-storage facilities at New Plymouth and Mt Maunganui but said it had no decision to enter the retail petrol market here.

Westpac boosted by equity gains: A spectacular 190 percent jump in WestpacTrust's first-half earnings owes as much to gains from the sale of its 48 percent stake in TV3 as it does to the takeover of Trust Bank in May last year.

PM unfazed by tough farm critics: Strong criticism from Northland and Southland farmers did not deter Prime Minister Jim Bolger from championing the the free market economy as he opened the Federated Farmers' conference in Wellington on Tuesday.

Judge lays out Phillips options: Ten years after some of the events recounted in the fraud trial of high-flying business executive David Phillips actually happened, the jury of six men and six women will bring to a conclusion the 13-weeks of trial in the High Court.
Carter vows more cuts in spending: Carter Holt Harvey has reaffirmed its commitment to cutting costs and improving efficiency in its current financial year.
THE PRESS
Waiting-list pain grows: Canterbury Health estimates it needs $27 million to $30 million to clear the backlog of patients on its surgical waiting lists. Page 1.

Public mood lifts; Labour still leads: Approval for the coalition government's performance has picked up slightly in the past month although Labour remains ahead in the party stakes, a poll suggests. Page 6.
Utilities group set to expand investments: South Eastern Utilities is looking to expand in utilities and infrastructure investments on both sides of the Tasman. Page 30.
Warehouse eyes info management for leads: The Warehouse retail chain is banking on the Internet and powerful databases to keep its tills ringing and customers happy. Page 27.
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
